gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two 12 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 batteries with a built-in BMS delivered more than their rating on a reviewer's bench. Michael Barton measured 1,378 Wh (107.7 Ah) from a Redodo 12V 100Ah at 5, 10 and 15 A. He measured an average of 1,350 Wh (104.2 Ah) from a Vatrer 12V 100Ah self-heating Bluetooth model over four runs at 10 and 20 A, with the BMS cutting off at about 9.6 V.
standout_why: The saved chat lists no searches and no results, so there was no rival page to read or compare against. ChatGPT's answer only explains in general terms what a BMS does and lists 4S/8S/16S nominal voltages. It names no product and gives no measured capacity, BMS cutoff voltage or cold-charge behaviour. Any named bench figure is therefore new. It is not a 3 because neither tested unit is exactly a SKU Dealectric lists.
decides: Measured capacity is above 100 Ah for both brands, so capacity does not separate Redodo from Vatrer. The useful measurements are elsewhere. On the Vatrer self-heating unit, Barton found the BMS cuts off at about 9.6 V, blocks charging below 0 °C (heat goes to the pad), resumes charging at about 4 °C, and the heater can draw 10–20 A, which is hard to supply from solar alone. He also found the official Vatrer app failed to connect. For a 48 V rack battery, no reviewer measured the Sun Gold SG48100P. The only named 48 V rack test I found, The Solar Lab's test of a Vatrer server-rack battery, measured a roughly 2-hour BMS reset after a 6,000 W surge trip. That is a reason to want a measured surge-recovery figure before picking a rack battery, not a verdict on the SG48100P.

findings.label: Measured capacity, Techtest.org (Michael Barton)
findings.source_title: Test: Redodo 12 V 100 Ah LiFePO4, wirklich 100Ah Kapazität? (ja)
findings.note: Published 2022-08-16. Charged to 14.6 V before each run, then discharged until the voltage fell below 11 V. Barton says over 90% of the capacity falls between about 13.3 V and 12.5 V. The article reports no weight, self-consumption, internal resistance or BMS trip current. This is the basic model with no low-temperature cutoff, not the Group 24 Bluetooth or self-heating SKUs Dealectric lists.

findings.label: Measured capacity, charge-test.com (Michael Barton)
findings.source_title: VATRER POWER 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 Battery Review: Bluetooth, App, Self-Heating at a Budget Price
findings.note: Published 2026-02-02. Measured with a DLB-600W electronic load down to 10.8 V. The tested unit uses the 329×172×214 mm 'automotive' case, which is not the Group 24 SKU Dealectric lists, so treat it as a brand-level data point.

findings.label: BMS low-voltage cutoff and cold-charge behaviour, charge-test.com (Michael Barton)
findings.value: Low-voltage protection trips at about 9.6 V and stays off until recharged. Charging is blocked below 0 °C (incoming energy goes to the heater) and resumes at about 4 °C. The heater can draw 10–20 A.
findings.source_title: VATRER POWER 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 Battery Review: Bluetooth, App, Self-Heating at a Budget Price
findings.note: Published 2026-02-02. The Xiaoxiang BMS app connected; the official Vatrer app did not work in Barton's test. He measured a voltage curve with about 90% of capacity between 13.1 V and 12.6 V and suggests stopping at about 12.5 V for longevity.

findings.label: Load and surge test, The Solar Lab
findings.value: Ran a 97 A load for just over an hour. Shut off under a 6,000 W surge and took nearly 2 hours to reset. Refused to charge or discharge after 24 h at −25 °C.
findings.note: The page names no author and gives no publish date (footer: © 2026). Dealectric does not list this battery. It is the only named 48 V rack test I found, included as a comparison point for the SG48100P.

findings.label: Measured capacity fade versus a 5,000-cycle claim, Panbo (Ben Stein)
findings.value: 104.69 Ah at cycle 1, 100.37 Ah at 100, 97.93 Ah at 300, 94.87 Ah at 600; predicted about 2,343 cycles to 80% at cycle 600
findings.source_title: Testing LiFePO4 cycle ratings, are they accurate?
findings.note: Published 2025-11-13, updated 2025-12-02. Cycled at 90% depth of discharge and 0.5C (50 A), charged to 14.2 V, with a capacity check every 100 cycles at 5 A to 10.5 V in a shop kept below 84 °F. This is a different brand, so it only shows that '5,000 cycles' on a spec sheet has not held up in a named long-run test.
